PENNSYLVANIA 
PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION 
HARRISBURG, PA  17120 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Public Meeting held February 1, 2024 
Commissioners Present: 
 
 
Stephen M. DeFrank, Chairman 
Kimberly Barrow, Vice Chair 
Ralph V. Yanora 
Kathryn L. Zerfuss 
John F. Coleman, Jr. 
 
 
PECO Energy Company Pro Forma Tariff Changes 
to Tariff Electric Pa. P.U.C. No. 7 
Docket Number: 
R-2023-3043673 
 
 
ORDER 
 
BY THE COMMISSION: 
 
On October 20, 2023, PECO Energy Company (PECO), Utility Code 110550, 
filed Supplement No. 36 to Tariff Electric Pa. P.U.C. No. 7 (Supplement No. 36), to 
become effective January 16, 2024.  On December 1, 2023, PECO filed to withdraw 
Supplement No. 36 and replace it with Pro Forma tariff changes to Tariff Electric Pa 
P.U.C. No. 7 (Pro Forma tariff).  PECO is requesting that the Commission allow it to file 
a tariff supplement consistent with the Pro Forma tariff changes to be effective on 
one-day’s notice when the implementation date for its Customer Care and Billing System 
(CC&B) is known. 
 
PECO states the proposed Pro Forma tariff reflects the elimination of Billing on 
Supplier Switch (BOSS Billing), changing the use of the customer’s account number with a 
new Electric Choice ID (Choice ID), and removal of the application of late fees to unpaid 
balances on final bills.

2
PECO states the proposed tariff changes are necessary to complete its plan to upgrade 
its current Customer Information Management System (CIMS) to a new customer 
information system, Oracle’s Customer Care and Billing.  PECO states the tariff changes are 
required to support applicable convergence of existing business processes and functionality.   
Pro Forma Tariff Supplement filing (a)(1). 
 
PECO currently uses BOSS Billing and generates a bill for every Electric Generation 
Supplier (EGS) enrollment or drop.  PECO states that with the elimination of BOSS Billing, 
customers will receive on-cycle bills that reflect all customer EGS switches within the billing 
period.  PECO states the new system will continue to support accelerated switching of 
suppliers within three business days, as well as the ability for customers to switch suppliers 
multiple times within the same billing period.  Additionally, PECO states that the elimination 
of BOSS Billing will reduce O&M expenses by approximately $11,000 per month.   
 
PECO states that it will replace customer’s account numbers with a Choice ID.  PECO 
states that EGSs will use this unique Choice ID for all supplier enrollments, drops, and 
historical usage requests.  PECO states that they will accept the old account number from 
EGSs for incoming transactions for a period of ninety days after implementation.  Response 
to TUS Data Request pg. 1. 
 
PECO states that it will no longer apply late fees to unpaid balances on final bills.  Pro 
Forma Tariff Supplement filing (a)(1) ¶¶1, 2, and 3. 
 
PECO avers that the use of a Choice ID and the removal of late fees on unpaid 
balances on final bills will have minimal to no impact on revenues or expenses.  Pro Forma 
Tariff Supplement filing (a)(5) ¶¶ 1and 2. 
 
PECO served the Pro Forma tariff on the Commission’s Bureau of Investigation 
and Enforcement, the Office of Consumer Advocate, and the Office of Small Business

3
Advocate.  Notice of the filing was published in the Pennsylvania Bulletin (53 Pa.B. 
7824) on December 16, 2023, with a complaint period ending on January 9, 2024.  No 
protests or comments have been received and no hearings have been held.   
 
 
The Commission agrees that the proposed tariff changes are required to support 
both the new Customer Care and Billing system and applicable convergence of business 
practices and functionality.  Upon review of the Pro Forma tariff, we find that the 
proposed modifications contained therein do not appear to be unlawful, unjust, 
unreasonable, or contrary to the public interest.   
 
 
Accordingly, we approved the changes requested in the Pro Forma tariff and direct 
that PECO file a compliance tariff to become effective on one day’s notice when the 
implementation date for the Customer Care and Billing system is known.  However, 
approval of this filing does not constitute a determination that this filing is lawful, just, or 
reasonable, but only that further investigation or suspension does not appear to be warranted 
at this time; THEREFORE, 
 
 
 
IT IS ORDERED: 
 
1. 
That the PECO Energy Company Pro Forma tariff changes to Tariff Electric 
Pa. P.U.C. No. 7 are hereby approved as to form and legality. 
 
2. 
That PECO Energy Company be permitted to file a tariff supplement on at 
least one-day’s notice to the Commission, containing the effective date, consistent with this 
Order. 
 
 
 
3. 
That a copy of this Order be served on the Office of Consumer Advocate, the 
Office of Small Business Advocate, and the Bureau of Investigation and Enforcement.
